newsitem.title: USA: Rig count up 18 to 845 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Rig count up 18 to 845 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas rose to 845 this week, up 18 from last week, and compared with a total of 765 a year ago, oilfield services company Baker Hughes Inc. said Friday.
The number of domestic rigs drilling on land rose by 15 to 716, while rigs working offshore rose by four to 106. The number of rigs active in inland waters fell by one to 23.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed an increase of 12, and Oklahoma, which showed an increase of eight.

A total of 319 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 28 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 39 to 514, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects rose by seven to 12.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 49 to 308 vs. 202 a year ago.
The rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for, not producing, oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 165 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Oct. 18, down one from the prior week,
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, was 92.2 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean remained unchanged this week at 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 105, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count rose by one to 561 out of a total fleet of 604, making the utilization rate 92.9 percent.
